title: Utilizing ChatGPT to Enhance Clinical Trial Enrollment
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of improving clinical trial enrollment by automating the initial step of identifying eligible trials from patient information in electronic health records. The authors focus on the challenge that clinical notes are unstructured, lengthy, and difficult to search effectively with standard retrieval methods.

The proposed approach uses ChatGPT (GPT-3.5) as an intermediate component in a retrieval pipeline. Given a clinical note, ChatGPT is prompted to extract patient-related information, disambiguate entities, handle negation in combination with a transformer-based model, and generate search queries for retrieving potentially eligible clinical trials. The study compares multiple prompt designs, including zero-shot prompts with different system roles and task instructions, and evaluates query effectiveness on two benchmark clinical trial retrieval collections.

The paper is not an education study; it does not involve students, teachers, or classroom implementation. The main findings are that ChatGPT-generated queries can improve retrieval performance over existing approaches under several prompting strategies, and in some cases even outperform human-generated queries. The authors conclude that ChatGPT has potential to support clinical trial enrollment by reducing human effort, while noting that its role is limited to structured information extraction and query formulation rather than direct decision-making.
quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical comparative retrieval study, but it is not an educational study and does not use a randomized or quasi-experimental design relevant to K-12 evidence standards. The paper reports benchmark evaluations rather than a rigorously controlled impact study on learners or schools.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests operational gains in a medical retrieval workflow, but it does not report educational impact or effect sizes that map to K-12 outcomes. Any impact is indirect and specific to clinical trial enrollment, so it is not evidence of educational impact.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT is used as an intermediate NLP tool to extract patient-related information from unstructured clinical notes and generate search queries for identifying eligible clinical trials.

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports that ChatGPT-generated search queries improve retrieval performance for clinical trial enrollment compared with existing approaches, and in some settings outperform human-generated queries. No student learning outcomes are studied; the practical contribution is reduced human effort in the trial-matching workflow and faster query formulation. Sample sizes and effect sizes are not reported in the abstracted text.
finding.measure: Retrieval performance for clinical trial search (e.g., ranking effectiveness on two benchmark retrieval collections)
